column1: # The Markdown subset, as rows its reader replays.
# against the reader. A row is a claim about the subset, so a change to the
# subset changes a row in the same edit, and a row nobody can explain is a
# defect in the subset or in the row. Every rule the reader refuses by has a
# row here that refuses by it, which that suite holds.
# Tab-separated, one row per line; a line opening with # is a comment, and a
#   accept  SOURCE  TREE            SOURCE is read as TREE
#   refuse  SOURCE  LINE:COLUMN  RULE   SOURCE is refused there, by the rule of that word
# In SOURCE, a backslash and n writes a line feed, t a tab, r a carriage
# return, a second backslash the backslash itself, and u with a hexadecimal
# code point in braces any character. No other backslash is read, so a
# backslash the Markdown itself holds is written twice.
# A TREE is written as the suite prints one, and is compared as text: blocks
# and inlines joined by one space, each holding what is inside it in square
# brackets. h1 to h6, p, code: and the fence's word, ul, ol: and its first
# number, li, quote, table with head, row and cell, and hr are blocks; a text
# in quotation marks, code and a text, em, strong, and link: with web, page or
# anchor and its target are inlines. Inside quotation marks a backslash, a
# quotation mark and a line feed are escaped as Rust writes them.
# A LINE and a COLUMN are counted from one, the column in characters.

# list's next item would be ends the list: never an item holding a rule.

# control characters and the space at its end are read before any block, and
